author: Wisnu Jesika
review_text: First, the waiting time was quite long we had to queue and wait for around one hour before getting a table. It was a bit tiring, but still understandable considering how popular this place is. One thing we really appreciated was that they provide free mineral water refills, which is a very nice touch and not something you always get, especially in busy places like this. The service was excellent all the staff were very friendly, polite, and attentive. They made us feel welcome and comfortable the entire time. There is a time limit of 1.5 hours for dining, but honestly, it was more than enough for us. The time felt fair and well-managed, so it didn’t feel rushed at all. For the food, we ordered the pork belly rice bowl and the ramen soup. Both dishes were good and enjoyable. In our personal opinion, we would rate the taste 8 out of 10 for both, not mind-blowing, but still tasty, well-prepared, and satisfying, matching our expectations. One small area for improvement would be the toilet, which could be cleaner and less wet/slippery. With such a nice restaurant atmosphere, improving this would make the experience even better. Overall, everything else was very good, and we left feeling very satisfied. We would definitely recommend Sensorium Canggu and would be happy to come back again.

author: Reyhwai WK
review_text: Sensorium Bali is truly exceptional. The food is outstanding—every dish is delicious with beautifully complex flavors that show great creativity and precision. The service is absolutely top-notch: attentive, warm, and professional without being intrusive. The atmosphere is elegant and inviting, making the entire dining experience feel special from start to finish. I will definitely come back whenever I visit Bali again. Wishing continued success to Sensorium well deserved!

author: Jessica S
review_text: We had a wonderful dining experience here. Every dish we ordered was thoughtfully prepared and full of flavor. The Crispy Quesadillas were perfectly golden and crunchy on the outside, with a rich and savory filling that made a great starter. The Pork Belly Rice Bowl was a highlight—tender, juicy pork belly with a beautiful balance of richness and seasoning, served with fragrant rice that complemented the dish perfectly. The Cold Rame Dry was refreshing and unique, with well-balanced flavors and a satisfying texture, making it a standout and memorable dish. The atmosphere was stylish yet comfortable, and the service was attentive and friendly. Overall, Sensorium offers a creative menu, high-quality food, and a great dining experience. Highly recommended!

author: Ping Boon (Bingoh)
review_text: The environment is really nice with a Muji-style vibe. Every dish is a delightful surprise to the taste buds 🥰 The staff there provide excellent and polite service. They ask if you have any food allergies and even guide you on how to enjoy each dish for the best taste. After the meal, they check if you’re satisfied with the food and end by sending you warm wishes for your journey💯 The waiting time was about 45 minutes. The tables are a bit close to each other, but it doesn’t affect the overall experience. The last row has a glass roof for natural lighting, but the sunlight can be a bit strong. Still, the staff were very kind and quickly brought us chairs so we could move to a shaded area👍

author: Tica Songrainy
review_text: POV: you’re “just getting brunch” and suddenly it’s the best meal of your trip. Tried the dry ramen, quesadilla, and pork belly rice bowl and honestly? No misses. Every bite said “trust the chef.” The vibe is cozy, chill, and always buzzing — which means yes, you might wait, but it’s part of the ✨experience✨. Staff are chill, helpful, and actually explain the menu instead of just nodding and disappearing. Prices are fair for the quality — this is not a scam brunch spot. 10/10 would come back. 10/10 would drag my friends here. 0/10 chance I stop thinking about that ramen. ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

author: 032. Ananda Putri Sudarmawan
review_text: I really enjoyed the service overall — it was especially nice to see the owner personally involved. The food was excellent; we ordered three dishes and every one of them was really good. One small note regarding the security service: when we arrived, it was raining and we came by motorcycle, but only guests arriving by car were offered assistance with umbrellas. I hope this can be improved so all guests receive the same level of care. Overall, it was a great experience and we will definitely be coming back.

author: Aida Anwar
review_text: The service is great, from the servers to the chef owner. All so friendly and look like they love what they do. Although, I feel the food can be improved. Ordered 3 mains and 1 side, the quesadillas is star of the show. The hummus dish lacked seasoning that is usually in a hummus, also I think the egg taste overpowers the overall dish. The fishbowl I was not a fan of as the rice is overcooked. I also wish there was less rice and more crunchy elements. I thought the food came really fast, good for sharing too. I would come back to try their other dishes!

author: Ahmad Fauzi
review_text: Love the positive environment around to dine in. All the staffs were attentive, and warm, plus the chef-owner being around and interacting with us- the guests. Foods were exceptional, and creatively driven, love the visuals, and this one actually tasted good in mouth too, not just in the eyes! Would recommend, and definitely coming back here in the future.

author: Eunice Chan
review_text: Food here in INCREDIBLE!! Menu is all Asian-fusion style brunch dishes. We had: - fishbowl: I absolutely loved this bowl, it’s like a poke bowl, but just so deliciously crafted - dry ramen: this was soooo good! there isn’t a lot of toppings but the flavouring and noodle texture was just spot on - miso pancakes: I was actually slightly disappointed in this given this seems to be super popular in the comments. The texture just wasn’t fluffy and the miso flavour didnt really come through It is extremely busy though so expect to queue. Also if you come as a bigger group, note that seating is only allowed when everyone in the group is present

author: Jo&Co Wanderlust
review_text: Sensorium is one of the best Asian-fusion spots in Berawa. The food was truly amazing : creative, balanced and far above the usual café standards. There’s always a line of people waiting outside, which already tells you how popular it is, and most of the crowd is Asian, which says a lot about the quality and authenticity of the flavours. Vibrant atmosphere, great service and definitely worth the wait.

author: Jessica Rusli
review_text: queue about 2 hrs! all the menu were very interesting. tried some asian fusion style dishes such as burgers, dry ramen, pancakes, salad etc. every meal were so flavorful and well seasoned. the presentation was very appealing and beautifully prepared. simply amazing!

author: Wil Budiharto
review_text: Foods are always good as usual. Love the ambience as well. The only downside is that they don't provide wifi for customers. Mobile Signal very sucks inside the restaurant. Limited to 1.5 hours (its okay) but No WiFi for customer is very harsh for Bali hospitality's standard...

author: Jun
review_text: Went at 12:30pm and waited around 30mins. Food was great, atmosphere was great. Service was good as well! The ice cream sandwich was so good that we forgot to take a picture! Note: there is a minimum spend of 150k per pax.

author: Resianing Marita
review_text: All the menus are very interesting and unique, which you cannot find in other restaurants. Very delicious, a combination of flavors that I have never tasted before. The staff is very friendly, the owner himself sometimes explains the food when it is delivered. For the price, it is very reasonable compare to what we get. At first it was estimated to queue for about 1 hour, but it turned out that 20 minutes we already got the table. The food is served fast. There is a little parking lot for motorbikes. it's better to drop off only by car or ride a motorbike. Overall will definitely come back again to try another menu 🥰

author: lydia aja
review_text: First time trying it because of the hype. Overall, the food was okay not amazing, but not bad either. If you’re curious, you can give it a try since everyone has different points of view and tastes. Just like hair color some people like blonde, some like black you can’t force taste, it’s subjective. FYI, dining time is limited to 1 hour 30 minutes. Since the seating is limited, it’s better to leave right after you finish eating because a lot of people are waiting to dine.

author: Sasha Octavian
review_text: ⭐ 9/10 – Unexpectedly amazing and definitely lives up to the hype I kept seeing Sensorium all over TikTok, so many people raving about it and I finally decided to visit to see what the fuss was about. Being the classic person that I am, I had to order the dish everyone mentions: the Brunch Dry Ramen. My French friend ordered the Okonomiyaki (didn’t take picture of it 😅) When I looked at the menu, I honestly became a bit skeptical. There were so many ingredients, textures, and elements in one dish that I started wondering how everything would come together. I was also slightly worried for my friend because he’s notoriously difficult to impress when it comes to food (blame the French palate 😂). But damn, once the food arrived, we both had huge smiles on our faces. It was amazing. Surprisingly harmonious, balanced, and fun to eat. Every bite had something different: sometimes crunchy, sometimes creamy, but always delicious. It turned out to be such an unexpected but wonderful experience. I’d easily give it a 9/10. My friend loved it so much he even brought his cousin for a second visit. Sensorium definitely lives up to the hype.

author: S Tang
review_text: Food this good is illegal. Impeccable flavour and friendly service. Will def come bk!!! Better come before 11am otherwise u hv to queue, we got luck and got seated right away. THE best scrambled eggs we ever had hands down. There’s hand sanitizer offered by the table, rly convenient.

author: Jonathan Lim
review_text: The greeter was very candid with the waiting time and our expectations were well managed. Was given menu while waiting outside. Food was served quickly and I can understand why this place is so likeable and popular amongst locals and tourists. Flavors and textures are balanced. It was crowded but tables were spaced well to still have conversation without feeling like a shouting match. Good kind of lively. Staff are friendly and accommodating too. Requested to have lettuce served separately for the beef quesadillas and waiter checked with the kitchen, and informed it is doable. Recommended 👍🏼

author: Andres Varela
review_text: Can’t believe I haven’t been here before! Yea, there was a bit of a wait (about 30 mins on Saturday at 2pm) so not too bad, but the food was 100% worth it! From the orange juice to the ramen, everything we tried was 10/10.

author: Radhitia Pradana
review_text: I think this is the 4th or 5th time we've treated our bellies here. From the small original spot to their current location , from FOMO to sustenance must-visit whenever we're in Bali. We always have a great time here. The food is consistently amazing, the staff are warm, friendly, and quick to respond, and the dogs are always adorable. The highest throne this time (tahta tertinggi) goes to the Crispy Quesadillas. The corn is still rockin', and the fish bowl is best enjoyed with nori — so we ordered extra nori to perfect every bite. Pro Tips: 1. Arrive at 8:50 AM, wait 10 minutes, and be among the first guests there. 2. Order extra double ground beef for Crispy Quesadillas. 3. Go to Sensorium on empty stomach. 4. Be kind and respectful.

author: Annastasya (Kei)
review_text: We stopped by in the afternoon for some dessert, and it was wonderful! First of all, the ambiance was perfect. You can experience an old Indonesian vibe inside the restaurant. As for the food, I ordered the pandan latte, which was delicious! The bailey's cheesecake was also pretty good. The service was good too.

author: Habib
review_text: Beautiful café with very good black coffee. Delicious cakes and pastries. I am grateful for finding a prayer room and ablution just behind the stage. What I really didn't like is that the pictures of naked men and women in the toilets.

author: Don Nguyen
review_text: **NOTE: We should have read the lowest ratings reviews on Google here before we went in. Those low ratings are Spot-on! Went here with my friend who was showing me around Fatahillah, aka Old Town Batavia in Jakarta. We were craving Italian and this little cafe eatery was near and right in the center square of attractions. Greeted by 2 front desk hosts who seated us at our table with 10 minutes. Our server name was "Ryan", whom I had tipped 50k IDR/$3 because I used to work as a waiter throughout College. After Ryan had taken our order, I had requested from one of the waitresses there named "Yulia" that I would like to order a bottle of water, so I could take my medication. After watching Yulia walk past us at least 3 times in a span of 20 minutes, and reminding her within 10 minutes after my initial request, she still did not bring us a bottle of sparkling water which I had ordered/requested. After I had realized she did not want to get me the water in a timely manner, I went up to the other waitress at the counter who didn't do anything but just stand there and told her I had ordered a water 20 minutes ago and have not received it and stated to her that if they don't want to serve us, we can leave. She then stated we would have to pay for our dishes (which we did not eat yet) and I said if I don't have my water I can't enjoy my meal. After she gave me an attitude I said this is not going to work out for us and just go ahead and charge us for the 2 smoothies we had, and forget the 2 entrees. She then said that I would have to pay for the entrees since they were in the kitchen being prepared. Fair enough, please get me my water I said. After me requesting to speak to their Manager "Neni", my water was promptly delivered to my table. Needless to say, our meal together with my friend felt very unhospitable and uncomfortable. Not a single time did any of these 3 servers come by to ask us if we needed anything else. Not to mention, we were charged before our dishes even came out. Our dishes were decent, not the best Italian I've ever had, but not bad. But for 2 dishes, my total came out to 854,000 IDRupiah, or about $54 USD for two people. I don't know if Yulia charged us correctly because she never delivered to us an itemized receipt of all the charges. I only have the receipt given from the credit card transaction, which is attached here. I will not recommend any Apple or Google colleagues of mine from California to come to this lackluster restaurant when coming to Jakarta to tour and sightsee this beautiful city. The service here at this restaurant is seriously lacking, and with much attitude. They are all about Money, and not the Customer experience. AVOID. BTW, this Batavia Cafe restaurant had just 2 tables the whole time we were there eating including us, so there is no excuse for poor service we experienced. We normally tip everyone, but this experience didn't even warrant our business.

author: Tiramisooo Tiramisooo
review_text: Café Batavia is a must-visit when exploring Jakarta Old Town. Once colonised by the Dutch, Jakarta Old Town has preserved its charming 17th century architecture and Café Batavia carries that same timeless vibe. ❤️ We stepped into a beautifully decorated space with floor-to-ceiling windows that let in the perfect dose of natural sunlight. The menu is extensive and the food is so good. “This is the best Mie Goreng that I’ve tasted,” says me. The springy egg noodle is fried to perfection and not oily at all. I’m still thinking of the Mie Goreng now. 🥹 #tiramisoooo #tramisoooojiaks #jiakjiakjiak #cafebatavia #jakarta #indonesiafood #miegoreng #jakartaoldtown

author: Evi Yuliati
review_text: "It's a must to stopped by" if you're in kota tua. The place is beautiful. Food is amazing. I had the best ox tongue and lychee tea there. Oxtail soup and latte is good as was. Very busy. Better make reservation beforehand to make

author: Grace Natalia
review_text: Loved my visit to Café Batavia! The ambiance is timeless — a beautiful colonial-style building filled with character and history. The food and drinks were excellent, with great presentation and rich flavors. Service was warm and professional, making the whole experience feel special. It’s the perfect place to enjoy a relaxed meal while soaking in the old-town charm of Kota Tua. Definitely a must-visit when in Jakarta.

author: Safyana Younas
review_text: Love it currently sat here after having finished our meal and waiting for the drinks! Everything was great and atmosphere was superb! My best meal so far in Indonesia. Service was absolutely fantastic, Apprillia was brilliant! Would definitely recommend for people to visit this place. Prices are reasonable and the music is lovely

author: Bobie
review_text: Great experience overall! The historic ambiance is charming, and the staff are friendly and speak English well. Loved every single dish we ordered—delicious and well-presented. Only downside: the ice cream portion was huge for just two people. Still, highly recommended!

author: Amy Lim
review_text: We were staying in Glodok area. So it's a must to visit this cafe. The building were constructed in 1830s. We went there for breakfast. It was a hot day so we were greeted by friendly staff that show us the way to up stair & another staff join in to bring us to our seat by the window. Wow! This place brings me back to the 60s with soft oldies being played as background. Very little thing of this place is so vintage. Let's talk about the food. At first the menu were brough to us with all wording. The waiter realise that I need aomething with picture, he qiuckly brough an tab or ipad to me to show the dishes in picture. From there we ordered our meals & drinks. For us, meal were good but the drinks so so only. I remember seeing other order dessrt. So we go for Ogy Ice cream small with 7 scoop 😍 & also poffertjes. We really love this dessert. We sitted there nearly over 2 hours, just enjoying the surrounding & chill out & unwind. I would said this is the best place so far for my trip in Jakarta, just relaxing & enjoying my breakfast💕 Price is on the high side but you paid for the environment. Food is good, drinks - okay, desset - yes please.

author: Vina Amira
review_text: The place is beautiful and iconic it really captures the classic old Jakarta atmosphere with vintage decor, high ceilings, and warm lighting. It’s cozy yet elegant, perfect for relaxing or hanging out with family or friends. I ordered Nasi Goreng Komplit, Mie Goreng Komplit, and Tuna Salad. The Nasi Goreng Komplit was flavorful and perfectly cooked, with generous toppings like chicken, egg, and satay. in addition Mie Goreng Komplit had that slightly smoky flavor and a nice mix of noodles, vegetables, and spices. i also ordered tuna salad, it was really fresh, and its dressing complemented the salad nicely. The staff were friendly, and the service was good once we were seated. However, the waiting list was quite long, so it took a while to get a table. i think this is the only drawback. Overall, Batavia Café is definitely worth visiting great food, a lovely ambiance, and an iconic place that truly represents Jakarta’s charm. i recommend this restaurant, especially for international tourists

author: Fitri Rachmadini
review_text: Café Batavia is such a unique restaurant with its authentic Dutch colonial building — it really feels like stepping back in time! The whole atmosphere gives you that nostalgic charm you can’t find anywhere else. Their cakes are delicious and properly made — definitely not disappointing. The price is a bit on the higher side, but totally worth it for the food and the one-of-a-kind vibes. ☕🍰🇮🇩

author: Оля Любарская
review_text: The food was really good, and for someone visiting from Europe, it felt very cheap. You can smoke on the first floor, but it didn’t smell smoky at all. We waited about 10 minutes for the food, though it was Monday and there weren’t many people. The desserts were also delicious and made right there. The staff were super friendly and spoke good English. We came back about an hour later after a walk, they called us a taxi and even walked us to the car.

author: Selvano Eduard
review_text: Exceptional! No other words. Atmosphere was nice with a view on the square, the food was also amazing but the service was the best in my trip Indonesia so far. Especially Novriyan, who handled the service like a true gentleman. Thanks for the experience!

author: Ianhung Lee
review_text: Instantly transport you back in time with dark wooden interior with colonial era touch on every corner. The establishment itself is elegant with a very attentive services. Food prices are on the higher side. There are plenty of seatings indoor but can be very occupied with tourists. Some area of seating can be loud with all the patrons chatting away while sipping tea.

author: Leo Khan
review_text: Amazing experience. Tasty food. Excellent service. My server spoke great English and gave really good recommendations of food and drink selection. I went there Saturday night and had almost no one in the restaurant. Everyone was nice and polite. Great live music with free one song request for the band. I will definitely come back again next time I'm in Jakarta. Highly recommend!

author: Yuhui LIN
review_text: I have been to the Cafe Batavia for twice. It is the most beautiful cafe in North Jakarta!! It has 2 floors and there are tons of photos and paintings inside, making the space very cozy. I recommend you stay here for a lunch or dinner. The price is also affordable for foreigners

author: Anna Safa
review_text: beautiful historical restaurant, a true fine brunch. it doesn’t taste authentic because the taste might caters more towards foreigners, it lacks seasoning and strong flavor that indonesia food holds. i got nasi goreng, ribs, and satay and others, it was okay, not the best. i also got strawberry juice, white wine and bintang beer. for the price, a fine brunch price, i wouldn’t say this is worth it. but it’s a nice one time visit. beautiful restaurant nevertheless, architecture and decor pieces is such a masterpiece. aircon is nice since kota tua is very hot. service is nice and helpful.

author: Sam W
review_text: Historical colonial style architecture. A must if you’re visiting Old Town Jakarta. Service was rather slow (we ordered one chicken and it took 30 minutes!) good cosy areas, well air-conditioned.

author: Vishhal K Bhusari
review_text: Appear polite in face but very rude ad core the staff at the entrance. Felt a cultural bias in treatment too. The staff at Bar super nice, polite and humble (welcoming) Came in with high expectations and disappointed First experience in Jakarta of the cultural bias

author: Lyda Hak
review_text: This place is a bit a high-end café where they expect you to spend. The more you spend, the better location you will be offered for seating. However, all staff are friendly, speak good English n good to enjoy the atmosphere where you can learn the colonial history of this building. The coffee itself was just fine, not as wow as I'd expected for.

author: Albert Yeo
review_text: Plataran Menteng is a delightful discovery despite my over 3 decades of transversing Jakarta. The deco, the atmosphere, the food and the service makes revisits for me a must. Very deserving of mention is the reasonably priced great tasting menu and the immaculately attentive service. Mr Kahman was of great help with our choice of food including some gluten free and other dietary challenges. Enjoyed a simply great lunch on a day when many parts of Jakarta was experiencing floods. 😄

author: Xinyun Huang
review_text: Top solo dining experience at a historic gem! The colonial architecture is stunning, and the atmosphere was made even more magical by the beautiful live Christmas piano music playing throughout the evening. I ordered the Iga Rawon (Black Ribs) with Green Rice and Salad Putri Dewi. The beef was incredibly tender, and the rich sauce paired perfectly with the aromatic rice. The guava salad was a refreshing surprise! The service from Kahman was exceptional! He was very helpful with the menu and gave some really good recommendations. He also recommended a look at the rooftop view - a breathtaking skyline night view in Jakarta. Honestly, the value for money here is incredible, especially compared to similar high-end restaurants in other major cities. True Indonesian hospitality at its best.

author: Joey “Joey123” Y
review_text: What a gem of a restaurant in Jakarta. We had a big table of 10. The service was on point, the decor was very tastefully done and immaculately restored building, inside and out. The rooftop bar was a big surprise and just divine. But most importantly, delicious local and authentic food, at a reasonable price. What a delightful experience and will definitely come again.

author: Yunsa
review_text: For the price, it’s definitely on the premium side—pretty typical for Indonesian cuisine in a restaurant setting. What’s really worth noting, though, is how perfectly balanced the flavors are, truly indulging anyone who loves authentic Indonesian dishes. From the photos uploaded, I’m sure you can already tell how delicious everything looks.

author: Mara Tayag
review_text: From the moment we stepped into Plataran Menteng, we were captivated by its exquisite yet cozy ambiance. The interiors strike a perfect balance between elegance and warmth, making it an inviting space for both intimate dinners and celebratory gatherings. The food was outstanding. We especially loved the Plataran signature telur asin platter, which was rich and indulgent. The Dendeng Batotok offered a delightful crunch and depth of flavor, while the Ayam Dwarmawangsa was a refreshing mix of savory and tangy. The Gado-gado was a comforting classic, beautifully presented and well-balanced. Service was superb. Sam, our server, was incredibly attentive and helpful—he patiently explained the menu and even gave us a tour of the restaurant, adding a personal touch that made the experience even more memorable. Overall, Platara Menteng delivers on all fronts: delicious food, impeccable service, and a stunning setting. Highly recommended for anyone looking to enjoy refined Indonesian cuisine in a beautiful space.

author: Dom Vito Briones
review_text: Delicious Indonesian food. The crispy fried beef and the short-rib were amazing, and all the salted egg treats had that lovely, punchy bite of salted egg flavor (which a lot of other places skimp out on). Atmosphere was wonderful. A wonderful home with a sophisticated but cozy ambience. If anything, I wanted to have seen more of the house. Service was fantastic. Staff was kind and friendly, and we were given a ride back to our hotel. Would recommend for anyone visiting Jakarta.

author: Lisa
review_text: I had a wonderful experience celebrating my birthday at Plataran Menteng. The service was exceptional, the food was fantastic, and the ambiance was absolutely lovely. My sincere appreciation goes to all the staff who made me feel so welcome and comfortable—it definitely makes me want to return! I was also pleasantly surprised with a delicious klepon cake accompanied by a thoughtful, personal note.

author: Tommy Chin
review_text: The place is absolutely gorgeous. I had the ox tongue satay, perfectly cooked, curry sauce was perfectly seasoned and packed with flavor. I sat on the ground floor at first, but my host, Sam, was incredibly kind to give me a tour around the establishment. I then had my dessert on the rooftop, which was the perfect way to end my stay in Jakarta.

author: Kyanna Soekardjo
review_text: Celebrated my birthday here for the sole purpose of “napak tilas j-hope” and was not disappointed! I was greeted very warmly from the very first start even with the valet service. The waiters and waitresses are all so nice and served us well. Special shout out to mas Sam who have catered my friends and I’s requests, must’ve took hundreds of pictures until we’re satisfied. And mas Kahman who have been so kind to j-hope when he visited and telling us beautiful stories about j-hope that we can’t help but shed a little tear! p.s. the rujak juhi is to die for! no wonder j-hope ordered more servings. All in all, the experience is immaculate. A birthday well spent <3

author: Didi huang
review_text: Elegant environment, nice food and good service. And the floor captain Mr Kahman is especially patient. Thank him that we had a wonderful night.

author: Tan TM
review_text: Beautiful colonial bungalow converted into a restaurant. Unfortunately the food was disappointing. Food was served cold and in tiny portions. I suspect the guys were hungry after dinner.

author: Yani Rafioedin
review_text: Having a private event for the third times at this restaurants, always happy to have their services , thanks to mas arifin and team for the excellence hospitality 🙏🏻🙏🏻

author: M Hoque
review_text: Terrible meal. The food was below average and the service was not attentive. We had a much better meal at Kaum Jakarta for excellent Indonesian food. Plataran Menteng is not recommended.

author: Susanna Lim
review_text: We had an unforgettable evening at Plataran Menteng, where every detail—from the thoughtfully curated dishes (We ordered the beef and pomelo salad, beef rawon, chicken satay and the grilled squid which tasted very good.) to the elegant colonial ambience—was executed with excellence. The setting itself is stunning, with beautifully preserved interiors and tastefully adorned dining spaces that tell a story of timeless charm. The serving staff were warm, attentive, and proactive throughout our visit, offering helpful recommendations and ensuring every aspect of our dining experience was seamless and enjoyable. We ordered the beef and pomelo salad, beef rawon, chicken satay and the grilled squid which tasted very good. A heartfelt thank you to Kahman for his gracious hospitality—his passion truly shone through as he shared the rich history of the restaurant and gave us a tour of the various floors, each uniquely decorated and steeped in character. It was a privilege to explore the space through his storytelling. We’re also incredibly grateful for the thoughtful gesture of arranging a car to take us back to our hotel. That extra mile made the entire evening feel even more special. A truly memorable experience—we look forward to returning on our next visit to Jakarta.

author: Lilyana Tan
review_text: Best restaurant in area Menteng. Nice place for meeting, family day, wedding, sangjit, birthday, etc. First coming in sangjit day. Slot parking is limited but can valet or park in cross road

author: Mariusz Skrzynski
review_text: Zuko was our host and tour guide after we explored Indonesian cuisine of Java . Thank you very much for this remarkable experience . We highly recommend it and definitely will be back Terimakasih baniak

author: Pat Benito
review_text: j-hope lead us to discovering & eating at this place and we were not disappointed. Such a wonderful ambience. The staff are very helpful, even when they realized we came because of j-hope’s influence. Lia was our server and she was really nice and attentive. The service was great, the food was so good. Personal fave is the lumpia bebek! Nasi Goreng Rendang is a good choice too~

author: Dada Linda
review_text: Very comfortable environment with very high standard delicious food！Definitely recommend trying！Dishes are all super flavorful and portion size is quite decent as well，love the mango salad fried chicken and house special panna cotta：）

author: Ritchie Sebastian
review_text: Specially crafted Indonesian cuisine. Using fresh & traditionally peculiar ingredients Loved by locals & foreigners. Very good venue for business meeting.

author: Man a
review_text: Top Place in Jakarta. Food Is great and not pretend tò be a moderno remake of traditiin. Servisse Is perfect and the colonial atmosphere make you dream a classic dinner of the 60'

author: Chloe Tan
review_text: Carbonara, sushi and fries was really good! Order the matcha cake dessert, its nice but abit too thick if finish the whole slice can share with people. Staffs and Thara was really nice and friendly

author: Happy Mama
review_text: I always come back here for the shoyu spice chicken . I loved the combination flavour of the homemade sambal with the chicken, mashed potato and rice . My son will always order the Odaiba big maxx burger. After main course, we will always have space for the bask cheese cake . You can choose Original and Yuri matcha . Both are delicious . We loved the tiramisu here too.

author: Pushpah Pushpah
review_text: The moment we enter until we pay the bill we really feel welcomed. The food recommendation were amazing and taste so good. Staff name Thara and Sasha provided an excellent service without a complaint and we are glad to tumble upon them, thank you The caramel pudding were simply awesome as this is our first time trying and it's simply excellent. Thanks TTR for making my day special.

author: szey t
review_text: Came here purposely for the cheesecake and honestly I totally get why people rate it 100/100. The texture is super smooth and creamy, and the taste is just amazing. Definitely worth the hype! We also tried two mains: 1️⃣ Lemon Cream Pasta The sauce was really refreshing and light which I liked. But the chicken... not so great. It had that weird taste, like it’s been sitting in the fridge for too long — not sure how to describe it, but hope you get what I mean. 2️⃣ Imperial Beef Curry The curry was rich and creamy, and the beef was super tender. Portion-wise only got 3 cubes of beef so a bit on the pricey side. Can added RM8 for an omelette Service-wise, no complaints at all. All the staff were super friendly and attentive.

author: DANIEL LOKE
review_text: I visited this restaurant on 28 November 2025 for lunch with my colleagues (around 1:40pm–2:40pm). The ambience was fine, but the food quality was disappointing. The miso soup and the TTR Napolitian (spaghetti) were extremely salty. A few hours after the meal, I started feeling unwell. Around 5:30pm I felt dizzy, and by 8pm I vomited and had diarrhoea twice. I went to a clinic, and after a blood test the doctor confirmed that I had a bacterial infection. The doctor also asked what I had eaten earlier. The only food I had before the symptoms started was the spaghetti and a spoon of salmon from this restaurant, so I am sharing this experience as a caution for others. I hope the management reviews their food handling and quality control. Unfortunately, I do not feel comfortable returning after this incident.

author: KY
review_text: Tried the original Basque cheesecake which it is really nice and delicious, especially with the side of cream that had a rich milk taste. The bar environment is also great, making it an enjoyable spot to relax with dessert.

author: Aisyah
review_text: First time tried out this restaurant. The food was scrumptious. The ebi roll was perfect. The burnt cheesecake was the bomb. Tiramisu cake was okay. The rice with omelette was a hit, no wonder it’s the signature of this restaurant. The price for food is reasonable too. The staffs were very welcoming and accomodating. Definitely love the warm hospitality. Definitely come again to try another menu.

author: Hristo Petkov
review_text: We visited specifically for the cheesecake after it was recommended by a local friend, and what a great recommendation! The cheesecake was absolutely delicious: creamy, soft, and perfectly sweet, all at a very reasonable price. We didn’t have dinner here, so this review is based solely on the dessert. The place itself was lovely, though a bit tricky to find, so you may need to ask for directions.

author: Rian Yamazaki
review_text: Shahmie was great! The raspberry matcha he made was really good. Highly recommend the bask cheese cake yuri matcha as well! 10/10 would come for desserts again 😆💖

author: Ji Yan Ong
review_text: Fantastic cheesecake (as always since we first tasted 10+ years ago) and great food. We were very well served by staff Danish throughout the dinner. He’s been offering high standards of services to us and being attentive to our needs. We enjoyed

author: Whitney Yee
review_text: Go there purposely for bbc. It's smooth creamy and for a reason the original one has a hint of chocolate fragrant. Slightly sweet. The matcha on another hand very rich in matcha taste, bitter and kaw, can be a bit jelak in the end. The lighting very dark in the snack zone, everyone can be seen switching on their camera light to have a look at the menu. The table light proves to be useless😅

author: Gabby H
review_text: Ordered the Miso Salmon and their signature Bask cheesecake. The Cheesecake is a must try for this place! Chill atmosphere and friendly staff. Would eat here again :)

author: Summer Gan
review_text: I used to love The Tokyo Restaurant's cheesecake — the one I had before covid was absolutely amazing. It was rich, creamy, and melted in the mouth effortlessly. Sadly, the current version feels quite different. The texture is now more solid and no longer has that signature melt-in-your-mouth consistency that made it so special. Still decent, but definitely not as memorable as before. I really hope they bring back the original recipe! Also tried the grape juice this time, but unfortunately it tasted quite bitter — not sure why. A bit disappointing overall compared to my past experiences.

author: Hayden Hayden
review_text: I would say their cheesecakes were awesome. Original cheesecake was so creamy and smooth. Tasted so good. Matcha cheesecake was a little bit solid but tasted good with a little salty taste. The only thing was too dark that day we went to, like having event and turned off most of the lights.

author: Sook Yee Chow
review_text: Amazed by their signature burnt cheese cake, silky smooth creamy texture . Love their Shoyu Spiced Chicken. It come with special made sambal , definitely a good combination. Great service and attentive staff.

author: Agus Syafika Raimon
review_text: Nice ambient & great food ! I really love their tiramisu & cheesecake. Love the vibes here, calm & romantic. Really have a great time here ! Will visit again for the cakes hehe ! Thanks Aiman for the great service ! So friendly & attentive 🤍

author: Altalia Sabri
review_text: All the dessert cakes were really good like seriously good! Their tiramisu, cheesecake, pudding, and everything else were just delicious. The rest of the menu was okay. I absolutely loved how the staff treated us. special shoutout to Aiman Danish who served us so nicely and friendly. Big star for him! Keep it up, guys! Will definitely come again. Highly recommended!

author: Samham Tam
review_text: Came here for the bask cheesecake after reading the reviews. The texture of the cheesecake was creamy smooth and paired well with the light whipped cream that came with it. It was a tad too sweet for my liking though. Ice latte was decent What impressed me most was the level of service. Serving drinking water and replacing it when the water glass was empty- all without prompting. Something you may not get at a restaurant these days. A big shout out to the service crew for the attentive service!

author: KM SY
review_text: Came across The Tokyo Restaurant on social media and heard many good things about their cheesecake, so I decided to give it a try by ordering a takeaway. The restaurant is tucked away in a corner on the fourth floor of Lot 10, so it’s not that easy to spot at first. I bought the Matcha Cheesecake, and it was really good — rich, creamy, and full of cheese flavour. The price is slightly on the steep side, but for the quality, it’s worth a try at least once.

author: Shang Yih Leong
review_text: Located inside the Lot10 Isetan food centre. Amazed by their matcha burnt cheese cake. Overall food taste also good.

author: Ong Shu Wen
review_text: Tried the Hokkien Mee (also known as prawn noodles) at this well-known spot in BM. The broth was rich and flavourful — definitely on the heavier side, which suits my taste and feels quite authentic. It’s a popular place for good reason. However, the coffee was a bit of a letdown — lacking in taste and depth. Still, if you're in the area, the noodles are worth trying.

author: Jessen Tan
review_text: Nice old house environment with modern touch. Hokkien mee is ok, a bit of sweetness tho. Reasonable price.

author: Philip
review_text: Local BM friend recommended this place, since I only left 1 breakfast left, I called the mixed Loh Mee/BeeHun that comes with prawn and chicken claw. I tasted it without the chili paste, the broth is really good, then with the chili broth taste even better. Coffee looks like Guinness Stout from a far, taste was Excellent or Amazing if your a caffeine addicts. loh Bak, though taste frozen food, good to enjoy with a large group of friends Garlic bread with half boil egg and coffee is also a must. If you are in Mainland, don’t missed this spot…..

author: pei yik
review_text: Hokkien mee is delicous and price was worth it.👍 Quite hard to find seats.

author: Forest Ang
review_text: This coffee shop has a small shop front but with dining area stretching to the very end of the house. Unique old coffee shop with old rusty cozy-looking atmosphere! For hokkien mee must try menu B with 2 prawns & 2 chicken legs @RM8 only.

author: Jenny Choo
review_text: The best Penang hokkien mee I have eaten so far (yes, I dare to say this). ;) On top of that, they serve nice artisanal drinks like cappuccino and matcha latte. Pair it with your flavourful hokkien mee, that’s the best of both (culinary) world!

author: Jessie Cham
review_text: Delicious and authentic Hokkien Mee, served in a long, old-style house by the roadside. Plenty of tables and chairs. Paid parking beside the house.

author: Oon Lan
review_text: Old house convert to Cafe the noodle delicious breakfast and koay teow soup is superb 。

author: Trisha T
review_text: Really love the prawn soup broth.. makes a good Hokkien Mee / noodles awesome braised phoenix claws too. Chicken feet / chicken metatarsus. Careful if u can't take chilli spice, it's a great kick. Good till the very last drop.

author: Khoo Jia Ming
review_text: nice noodle but Bad services Dear HOKKIEN MEE STALL, bear in mind that Penang not only have you this hokkien mee, mind your attitude

author: Oliver Tey
review_text: MUST try the famous Hokkien Mee and the brew coffee. KTT with every sinful bits was as tasty with sizable portion served. Somehow waited very long for the coffee. It seem The barrister had missed out our order. Saw that apologetic puppy face on our cappuccino when served. Surprised that it's mouth opened when kaya toast was delivered a few minutes later. Seem try to apologize where our order was delayed🤣🤣 A joyful breakfast with yummy food n coffee. Surprise there are seats in the open air back lane if you want a different ambient. Recommend to visit when in BM

author: kathy.cheang kathy.cheang
review_text: Must try Hokkien noodle, prawn noodle with many ingredient, RM9 per bowl reasonable price. Good coffee cheap price, 3 mix signature recommeded too, taste like hokasai.

author: Jaynian
review_text: Honest review from a local. Hokkian mee is ok, though hokkian mee in the other corner of the street tastes better. The chu chang fen is good. One thing to note is that if not specifically mentioned, they will serve the big bowl. The young boss is impolite to elderly persons, a common issue for old brand business.

author: Andrew Yeoh
review_text: There are two main stalls. One sells Hokkien mee while the other one specialises in koay teow thng. The Hokkien mee comes in a full set with a small piece of pork ribs, two medium sized prawns, egg and two chicken feet. Taste-wise, it is quite good. The broth is thick with nice consistency and not too prawny. The broth is slightly spicy which is much to my liking. The koay teow thng comes with fish balls and minced meat balls. In my opinion, it is not great. The place is very popular. There was quite a long waiting time. The shop is actually quite non-descript, rather long and narrow. There is a parking lot just at the corner which charges RM2 per entry.

author: 茉莉Jasmine
review_text: If u r the 1st time having here and just pick the food photo 😂 Hokkien mee is serve with 2pcs of prawns and 3 pcs of chicken feet, RM 8 per bowl and if you want to add on one big fishball will cost RM 9/bowl. Ordered one cup of cappuccino and they craft a cutie cat there 🐱 Egg on toast is like ipoh egg sandwich 蛋治 and you can add how much the soy sauce & pepper as you like.

author: Ice Ice Kitchen “Ice Ice”
review_text: Coffee is completely failed!👽 Ordered coffee less sweet but end up received a cup of coffee tastes like sugar water. It has zero coffee taste. Feedback to them and they took back my coffee to modify. But still bad. Worst coffee ever I have had in Bukit Mertajam. Half boiled eggs maybe ok. Although the eggs are almost 80% done, still acceptable by me. However, my friend couldn’t accept. So this is really personal preference or I have already lower down my expectations after my bad coffee is served. Guang Xi Hokkien Mee is alamak. Was recommended by local friend to give it a try. Took me a while to place my order as there isn’t and proper queue. The stall owner don’t even look at me until I wave my hands and ask her how should I place my order. She ask me to look at the menu. I have actually decided my meals and I told her what I want. She didn’t reply me and I repeat once again. I think she is over confident with her memory. To cut short, I went over 3 times and finally received my noodle. I can easily get something better outside. Hence, no next time. Environment is wow. The environment is unique and I’m really impressed when they are serving both eastern and western coffees. Maybe I should have ordered western instead. Less chance to go haywire. Conclusion ~ Read more reviews before heading down. I’ll not come back for 2nd times for sure.

author: Peter
review_text: Best hokkien mee in bm area. A lot of side dish choices.

author: Joshua Yap
review_text: Good Penang hokkien mee (RM 6) for the basic. Kopi ais was Rm2.40. Much cheaper compared to KL. A good bowl of noodles. Ample of tables and chairs behind

author: Millie Voon
review_text: A quaint breakfast place with choices of basics toast with half boiled eggs/sandwiches with brewed or local coffee, anchored by Koay Teow Thng hawker food.

author: Chong SV
review_text: Excellent food, no complaints there. My only concern is that the toilet hygiene is in desperate need of attention and needs to be addressed by the owner.

author: Eric Foo
review_text: Pretty good Ramly burger place. They also have premium beef patty burgers and fried chicken sandwiches. Like typical Ramly burgers, it is drowned in sauce, but the coleslaw makes a nice difference from others.

author: Kesiga Morgan
review_text: We bought Pattaya chicken burger special last night. We were totally fine and healthy before our meal but after our meal, we’re now ended at hospital for diarrhoea and vomit due to food poisoning. Actually not only us, there are also few reviews posted regarding the food poisoning since past few months. The reason why I’m posting this is to alert the owner. I’m not blaming or wanna ruin the business, but I thought the owner should know so you can check your ingredients, food storage, and cleanliness - something went wrong. Please make sure that this doesn’t repeat to any other customers. Thanks.

author: MiLaa
review_text: We tried burger ayam pattaya and burger ayam combo today. The taste was good but I would not say it was excellent. Their coleslaw is bland and too watery. The reason why I'm giving 4 stars instead of 5 star is, at the end of finishing the burger we do have the slight puke feeling because the burger was too soggy. Otherwise it is a decent roadside burger. Price wise I'm not sure if it is reasonable because it cost us RM29 for burger ayam combo with burger pattaya.

author: Sarah Lee
review_text: A famous burger stall located in Sg Dua which served homemade patty burger and Ramly burger. The Ramly burger here was pretty standard- nothing much to shout about and was rather messy to eat around as it was doused with sauce. A better option would be the grilled beef burger which was flavourful and peppery. The burger is huge and comes with a 150gm patty. The beef patty was slightly overcooked but paired well with the sauce. Heard that queue can be quite long during peak dinner hours.

author: Faruq Mokhtar
review_text: Surely one of my favourite burger stalls in Penang. I wouldn’t say it’s the best burger in terms of taste, but it’s delicious nonetheless. The most important part is that it’s reliable and the taste is always consistent. Definitely my go to burger all the time.

author: Henry Tan (Xuan)
review_text: It’s my go to place for Ramli burger whenever I feel want to have one. 1 thing special about their burger is they will give coleslaw instead of cabbage. And I found 1 thing nice for people that want slightly lesser carbo 😂 you can ask them not to put bread, or there is another option which is burger cincang, they will put slices of burger meat, hot dog and egg, then top with coleslaw’ and some veges, plus cheese and sauce on top 😍 Nice burger stall to go 👍🏻 Btw it’s a roadside stall so no place to dine in.

author: Justin Vaughn
review_text: I am only traveling here a few days so I had this two days ago and this is a MUST try. Great burger for very fair price. The flavor is so good! Im going back tonight even though I just went two days ago.

author: Desmond Boon
review_text: Not worth the wait.. so overrated and the way they handle burger and squeezing almost whole bottle of cheese is just crazy.

author: Jerem Chang
review_text: There's usually a long queue here, but it's worth the wait. My personal favorite is their grilled beef burger.

author: Daniel Ooi
review_text: This shop provide call order.... But if having few order in 1 call, u have to call 1 by 1. The owner/seller will end the call once 1st burger was done, then u will need to call again. They actually end call very suddenly.... Without saying bye or anything else, they won't asking that's all..... Food is good, but service like really poorr..... I know they having a superb sale, but they seems like not actually appreciate customer..... That's what i feel.... Kinda sad

author: AMRI SYUKRI
review_text: I order 1 with vegetables and 1 without. After this i got 2 without vegetables. Long to wait my burger although i already order 20 minutes from Whatsapp and still wait some more minutes.

author: edmund goh
review_text: It may not look like much but the taste is good. Its a regular Ramly butger which should look messy and taste great. Taste better than the plain burgers served by big M.. Burger special recommended.

author: Arkib Ilmu
review_text: Taste wise its average. The queue time is super long. But to be honest it's a gamble to eat here. Sometimes it's okay, sometimes you will get bonus diarrhea the next morning after eating the burgers because all the dust and dirt from the road gets mixed into the food. Would recommend eating elsewhere for better and cleaner foods. Service isn't the best either. Customer service quality is out of the window with occasional rudeness towards customers. Probably became like this because they have too many customers now and won't mind losing 1.

author: Funny George
review_text: Very bad attitude, I didn't know that customers pay after the burgers are done over here. So, I directly scanned QR Duit Now and paid the money after making orders then they are very unhappy and didn't even said 'thank you'. What's wrong with I paid first? Am I wrong?

author: eleq
review_text: love the fried cken burger .. have to wait quite some time for the order to be done

author: Law Yin Zhi
review_text: Best burger I have eaten in Penang. Came back for it again!

author: CP Goh
review_text: Expect to wait for 20 minutes plus at least ... do recommend to order it in advance via call to avoid unnecessary waiting ...

author: Khye “Joshua” Khoo
review_text: This is one of the best street burger stall that can compete with Big Names, their burgers is nicely cooked, well-seasoned and price is very affordable! Always long queue and orders is plenty. Expect to wait >30mins if long queue, but I think the waiting is worth it for their burgers.

author: elcoco enjaco
review_text: We ordered one beef burger special and two chicken burger specials. They were both delicious and IMHO the best I've had in Penang. We didn't have to wait long even though they were quite busy. This was due to their well thought out system. I couldn't believe how reasonably priced their menu is.

author: Hao Yan
review_text: Food was nice but the staff was rude. Im just asked twice “berapa ringgit?”, the staff speak very quickly and impatient tone then said again “aku sudah ckp dua kali dah”, I just heard “brahbrah setangah” Hey bro, I already speaking Malay nicely with you hang ni beri aku sikap ini!?? If I already knew the price I won’t asked the amount again for double confirm..

author: Siu Bernice
review_text: Been here a couple of times, and today I ended up here again because my visitor *insisted* we makan here. 😂 As usual, the place was hot, packed, and buzzing with people hunting for food. You’ll also get tissue sellers going table to table — some quite persistent. Food options? Endless. Biscuits, buns, noodles, CCF, durian, drinks — you name it, they probably have it. So many choices, you’ll definitely find something to try. We had the vegetarian curry mee, the famous CCF, and the Bintang Cham drink and Teh. Verdict: honestly, all quite mediocre for me. Didn’t finish the food. CCF is RM2.80 per piece, curry mee RM11. (BUT this is just my personal taste — plenty of people around me were happily eating, so don’t take my word for it. Go try and judge for yourself!) We also ta-pau’ed the miniature wine chicken pau, Bun Choon egg tart, nian gao, and yam kueh. The nian gao was good — I like the original version without yam or sweet potato. The egg tart was good too. Go try this place and eat your way to a happy tummy !!

author: Debbie Li
review_text: I didn't understand the hype about this food court. We ate at the most popular Ahfook Yong Tau Fu stall and found it to be grossly overrated by YouTubers. Yes it is cheap but the quality of ingredients is low and the whole thing was really tasteless. I also tried the fabulous popiah. It was just ok and lacking in complexity of ingredients and crispness. I think I've had better ones in Singapore. The triple layer lava cake - fun to eat but very oily and lacks depth of flavours. I have to agree that the taste and atmosphere here is authentic Malaysian. It's hot, cheap and bustling. Maybe it's still worth one visit just for the experience. But make sure you get there early before lunch because some of the popular stalls did sell out when we got there at 1pm.

author: Jackie
review_text: Managed to score a clean, cool table tucked all the way inside this huge and humid hawker centre near Bunn Choon (egg tarts). Tried the vegetarian laksa as there was no queue. Didn’t taste like the laksa I’m more familiar with and instead had an Indian curry taste.Still, it was rather nice. Uncle’s Fresh Coconut here is a must try! It’s huge, icy and refreshing, and best of all, the metal spoon to scoop the tender sweet flesh at the end of the meal was the best desert on a hot afternoon. The Yong Tao Fu was okay but the freshly made chee cheong fun that went with it - I can eat 5 servings and ask for more. Just a simple drizzle of soy sauce and sesame oil and it’s like so soft yet chewy, light not stodgy like most rice noodles. Heavenly yum yum.

author: The Travel Hunter
review_text: I recently visited ICC Pudu Food Centre and was thoroughly impressed by the wide variety of authentic local dishes available. Among the many options, I tried the Lala Bee Hoon, Curry Niang You Hu, Hainanese Coffee, and Fried Fish Rice, and every dish left a lasting impression. The Lala Bee Hoon was light yet flavorful — the clams were fresh, and the broth carried a natural sweetness with a hint of seafood richness. The Curry Niang You Hu stood out for its aromatic, creamy curry and tender stuffed fish pieces, a perfect balance of spice and comfort. The Fried Fish Rice was another highlight — crispy on the outside yet juicy inside, paired beautifully with fragrant rice and sambal. To complete the meal, the Hainanese Coffee was strong, smooth, and perfectly roasted, delivering that classic old-school kopitiam flavor. What makes ICC Pudu Food Centre truly special is not just the food, but the vibrant atmosphere — a perfect blend of tradition, efficiency, and community spirit. Prices are reasonable, portions are generous, and every stall feels passionate about what they serve. This is truly a five-star destination for anyone who loves authentic Malaysian flavors.

author: Ricky Hwan
review_text: To anyone who enjoy eating n all kinds of delicious food...Is a must come place... Is a very crowded place on the weekends n just have to wait for seats... There's really alot of stores around with lots of delicious food to choose..so is good to walk around first before deciding 😋 on what to eat...

author: Alvin Lim
review_text: Cheap and good. Just have to bear with the "sauna like" environment. Amidst the seemingly chaotic vibe, there is a "system", like how the cleaners quickly clear up the tables and how the diligent drinks stall workers go around taking orders and delivering the right orders! There are many many stalls and can be overwhelming but I have my own favourites. Really enjoyed the yam cake, the steamed promfet fillet and the seafood rice porridge! Also the very yummy spring roll (popiah) with very nice "textured" filling and cost less than Sgd$1 per roll! You must walk all the way in and you will find the stalls with the authentic hawker fare. Also, some of the stalls have very (PRC) kind of sign boards. That's another indication of authenticity of the fare they are offering. Breakfast hours only (most stalls closed by noon). For Singaporeans, take note that there is table service and you do not need to return tray! Amazing.

author: James Shiju
review_text: A bustling hotbed for locals here to congregate for breakfast and lunch mainly, due to its large concentration numbers of food stalls offering a wide range of mainly local Chinese local hawker fare. A wide range of choices to select depending on one's inkling. Overall all the ones that I tried were pretty good and authentic. Despite their busyness, the operators were still relatively polite and friendly, partly I supposed due the the competition of a few repeated food type stalls. The ordering system here is self service and pricing is reasonable. I came at a non peak time, and was able to find certain seating spots were more airy at the edge with openings (no hemp in) than those internal spots. I supposed, one would not have such luxury at peak and packed times, as this place is obviously very popular among the locals and visitors. The set up here is quite basic, with the attention focused on the food. I was quite surprised that the floor is just cement screed finished and not tiles for eater facilities, though overall the place is considered quite clean and tidy.

author: Lee Zhao
review_text: Visited this bustling local hawker center for lunch. The ambiance is classic and busy—lots of energy, plenty of tables, and you get the true experience of local Malaysian food culture here. The Food: I ordered the Ginger Rice Wine dish with Prawn and Pork (RM13.00). • Value (3/5): At RM13, the price is a little on the higher side for a hawker stall, so expectations for flavor execution are raised. • Ingredients (4/5): The ingredients themselves were generous and looked fresh—good portion of sliced pork, decent prawns, and a nice, thick, savory egg gravy. • Flavor (2/5): This is where it fell short. Despite being a 'Ginger Rice Wine' dish, the dominant, warming, and pungent flavors of the ginger and wine were almost non-existent. The food tasted surprisingly "normal" and lacked the punch and character a signature item should have.

author: Jasper Lei
review_text: Huge selection of food choices Pretty great ventilation and over not hot at noon timing - YTF was awesome - Fried fish soup noddle was great w thick yellow wine taste - Wanton Mee with melt in your mouth charred fatty char siew is heavenly - Nasi Lemak pretty average with extremely oily fried chicken dripping oil on the rice 😂

author: Chong Yin Koon
review_text: The Imbi pork noodle kennot. Too bland and expensive for the quality of pork. The other stuff like apam balik and keng cheow Hailam coffee are awesome. I will try the Hailam chicken rice and Teochew fish noodle next time. Oh yeah, the water here quite dirty. Service of table kinda slow at times because lack of manpower. Understandable. Atmosphere. Weekday is good (before and after the peak rush hour of lunchtime). Weekend is overcrowded and hard to find table to sit down and eat.

author: Teng Sook Yin
review_text: First time visited this huge and obviously very popular hawker centre. Very impressed with the variety of food available. Eventhough there was a huge crowd, there was no problem finding a table. We tried the beef noodle and curry noodle Both were good. We bought the dumplings for breakfast the next day. They were very delicious with lots of meat. Yum yum. Will definitely go again, even went round to check which are the popular stalls (with long queues). Haha...

author: pui kuen Yap
review_text: One of my favorite breakfast spot. Simple breakfast make you happy. How ever many people will said ICC is a tourist place but is a good place to have a good foods.

author: tm sii
review_text: A huge food court which is very crowded and humid particularly during weekends, patrons are attracted by the large numbers of stalls offering a wide range of food choices to fulfil one's taste buds. Certainly a place for food lovers who like vibrance and don't mind the heat and queue even for a table. Best to come during week days. Private parking nearby costs RM5 per vehicle.

author: Eason Wong
review_text: Great choices of local foods and drinks with authentic taste. Must visit place for foodies who want to explore local hawker foods. The venue cleanliness and hygiene need improvement.

author: Lucas Chan
review_text: Hawker centre. Nice melting pot for local food, so much variety. Except that there’s no aircon but well ventilated, room temperature. Clean place. Advisable to come early as it will be crowded during peak hours.

author: darren Chia
review_text: Great for breakfast and brunch. Most of the popular stalls start early and may sell out before noon, so it’s best to come early. Prices are reasonable, and you get to enjoy hawker food in a cleaner, more comfortable setting . Weekend mornings are crowded, so expect some waiting time or sharing tables. Overall, ICC Pudu is a must-visit for foodies looking to enjoy classic Malaysian flavors under one roof.

author: Lee Kokliang
review_text: This was the worst tim sum I have eaten. Didn't expect such poor quality. The food was cold, especially the prawn Chee Chong fun which was hard, obviously it was frozen and put to steam for a while. Told staff to re-steam. The chicken feet was hot on the outside but could feel the cold inside. Siew Mai meat was too hard. Won't be back. The staff were busy playing handphones and not interested in work. Anywhere else in Malaysia is better.

author: Ngọc Hải
review_text: nice staff, good food especially hainan chicken rice and milk tea, milo. I want to eat the sticky cake but 8.30am it open and we come in 7am so they dont serve. It may be hot because not all area has air conditioner. Food really cheap at about 30rm for all this but just paid in cash or touchngo wallet no card

author: Sean T
review_text: ICC Pudu is really a hidden gem for food lovers. The HK roast here is absolutely delicious – the char siew melts in your mouth, tender and flavorful, while the noodles are perfectly bouncy and coated in an awesome sauce that ties everything together (see picture!). Auntie Mei’s crispy Popiah is another highlight. It’s super crispy on the outside and packed full of fresh, tasty ingredients inside. Every bite gives you that perfect crunch and flavor (see photos). And don’t miss out on Wang Fatt’s drinks and snacks – the iced Hainan coffee is rich and refreshing, and it pairs so well with their toast bread, which is crispy on the outside and soft inside (see photo). Overall, ICC Pudu is a fantastic spot to enjoy a variety of delicious local eats all in one place. Highly recommend checking it out if you’re around the area!

author: Eddy Hoo
review_text: The food here seriously is not up to rated ratings. We (me and my family) came here to try out those by food recommended. Seriously, it didn’t come near to what rated. The air quality here is also bad, seems smoky and warm. Means their exhaust ventilation system either is not functioning/ not maintained (services) or the kitchen hood exhaust wasn’t design to cater for this situation. From I can say, it is OVERLY rated. I can understand and agree that everyone has different taste buds. The food taste is normal nothing special but there are many varieties (choices).

author: Tan Adrian
review_text: I’ve been to KL several times and always wanted to try this place. This time, I finally came with my family and the elderly — but unfortunately, it turned out to be a huge disappointment. I strongly urge everyone not to order their claypot rice. It completely lacked fragrance and flavour, the rice was bland, and the lap cheong (Chinese sausage) was of poor quality. Honestly, they’re not professional at all in preparing claypot rice — it just didn’t have the authentic taste or aroma expect. The only saving grace was the sambal stingray and sotong, which were quite decent and had good flavour. However, the seating area was cramped, making it uncomfortable to dine in, and the staff were unfriendly. Overall, the experience was disappointing from both the food and service side. Definitely not worth the hype or revisit.

author: HoodlumHavoc Gaming
review_text: Food is excellent! A must try when visiting KL. Try the chicken claypot and the grilled fish. You may be seated outside, and they may have long queue sometimes, depending on day and events. Not sure but auntie who is like the boss is a little annoying. We were trying to ask for additional spicy sauce or flakes. But she declined and talked to there guy at there language (not sure what they are talking sbout) but it seems they are making fun of our request because the fish sauce is already a little spicy, we just wanted more spice. But it seems they made fun of our request. (But again not sure what they are talking about, i can only be sure that she declined and said no no no). KL is humid and hot most of the times, so if you are not the person who is comfortable eating outside (humid with street noise, people walking, cars around) this might be uncomfortable for you. Just be ready when you dine here coz experience is not the usual dining experience. Lots of options around who offers almost same menu so you may wsnna try others too if you want. This is our exp, you may have diff exp. Just sharing and being honest

author: Timothy E.
review_text: One of the best claypot rice in the heart of KL! The flavour, texture and that smoky taste are sooo good. Also tried their Portuguese grill fish - super tasty and worth a try. Prices are pretty decent too. If you’re around Petaling Street hunting for good food, this spot is a must-try!

author: Manjit Sangha
review_text: Just absolutely brilliant food, like a biryanis but much better. Crispy spicy delight with an egg on top wow, cooked for all to see, fantastic. Had clams and a prawn dish just so fresh and once I stirred the clay pot the rice with crunch and soft texture was divine. 10/10.

author: Dao Viet
review_text: So, the hype was way too much. Hardly any chicken, one lonely slice of Chinese sausage for decoration, and the rice—well, let’s just say it couldn’t decide if it wanted to be cooked or raw. All fame, zero substance. Honestly, it doesn’t even come close to a simple claypot rice you’d find in Saigon’s Chinatown. Final verdict? Worth a try just to say you’ve tried… but once is more than enough.

author: Emily
review_text: Came here for dinner at 8pm, crowded and had to queue for around 15mins. It was hot and humid. Better bring a portable fan. We ordered a large set, comes with claypot chicken rice, tomyam seafood platter (added petai for rm5), stir fry vege with bean sprouts and a peanut soup. Also ordered 3 drinks, coconut, honey lemon & lemon juice. Total bill was RM113. Overall, it wasn't that great, just average. The only thing special here was this shop only opens at night. Will I come back here to eat? Nah, but you could come try it and just get to the touristy feel of having local food.

author: Siewyen Ng
review_text: Claypot rice is nice and tasty. Grilled lala and stingray not so nice. Food serving is fast. Staff not so friendly and need to sit outdoor.

author: Grace Tay
review_text: It was average… we ordered medium claypot rice with vegetables as sides. The queue moved fast, and we also got our food rather quickly. However it’s not very memorable ; grilled stingray were available too but we didn’t order

author: Beatrice Zhang
review_text: Food was average, the service was too bad. The queue was long, we waited around 20 minutes to be seated. The staffs were really loud. We consisted of 9 person so they needed to combine the tables for us but one of the owner slamed the chair for us instead of putting them nicely. It was raining heavily. Then one of the staff tried to adjust the tent roof right above where we sat and splashed water right to my friend. He didn’t wait for us to finish eating to adjust it, nor did he apologized afterwards. Another staff apologized for his behalf instead. The owner just laughed and didn’t say anything to us. Definitely not recommended.

author: Simon Koo
review_text: Great food and prompt service. Ordered the claypot chicken rice for 2-3 pax and a stir fried vege. The small piece of salted fish adds aroma to the claypot. Take note that it's more hawker style with functional table and chairs, Not for those who prefer restaurant style settings.

author: Evan L
review_text: We noticed someone reviewed that they had to wait 20 minutes for their claypot rice. Honestly, we would’ve happily waited that long, usually that’s a good sign the rice is cooked fresh in the claypot, not just pre-cooked rice with some raw chicken thrown in. But sadly, that wasn’t what we got. There was no crispy, crusty rice at the bottom, which usually means they probably used pre-cooked rice. On top of that, the rice didn’t have much flavour, even though they poured quite a lot of dark soy sauce over it. We ordered the medium-sized claypot (RM25, June 2025) but only got a few small pieces of chicken and just a couple of thin slices of Chinese sausage - it felt a bit stingy. The server didn’t even ask if we wanted salted fish, which we thought was usually part of a proper claypot rice. She only asked if we wanted to add an egg. Overall, the claypot rice just didn’t live up to expectations. It seems like the place is more popular with tourists than for the quality of the food. They did have other options like BBQ stingray, but we didn’t try those.

author: Eugene Chia
review_text: You have to Q and order outside before they seat you. The food came faily fast around 5 minutes. The Claypot chicken rice with lap cheong is fragrant and the taste is ok. 1 sour plum drink + mix vege small + Medium claypot chicken rice rm38 Reasonable la d price in a touristy area.

author: Magga Andika
review_text: I ordered claypot chicken rice, but sadly it wasn’t served hot. Looks like the rice was pre-cooked and just reheated with the chicken. The flavor didn’t come out as it should, and even the egg took quite a long time to cook.

author: BeerBiie WCK
review_text: The Portuguese grilled fish was quite good, with a lovely aroma of chili oil and spices. I ordered the stingray, and it tasted excellent, and the squid was fresh. This menu I recommend. For the clay pot menu, I recommend adding Chinese sausage (gunchiang). The sweetness of the sausage perfectly balances the savory flavors. As for the vegetable dishes, I found them a bit bland.

author: Yan Wai Wong
review_text: Came here on a Sat night 10pm. A little of a queue. Im surprised by the crowd. Spent RM60 Claypot rice turned out super underwhelming. Didnt taste any salted fish at all. Rice did not have flavour. Rice not very charred. Please do not bother to try this place. The veg was ok, seafood was so-so.

author: Chef’s
review_text: I can’t say this is the best claypot rice, but the chicken marinate with favourite is amazing, juicy and tasty make me keep going well with the rice.

author: Voon Wong
review_text: Hong Kee Claypot Chicken Rice in KL’s Chinatown is known for its signature claypot chicken rice, best enjoyed with Chinese sausage and a crispy, charred rice bottom. Cooked over a charcoal fire, the dish has a smoky aroma that enhances the tender, flavorful chicken. Pair it with their refreshing grass jelly drink for a classic combo. While some diners praise the rich flavors, others note inconsistencies in the rice texture and service. The no-frills eatery offers both outdoor and air-conditioned seating, making it a convenient stop for a traditional meal in the heart of KL.

author: Meera Nair
review_text: Finally tried Hong Kee Claypot Chicken after having it on my list. The claypot rice was decent, though I personally prefer a stronger char. Not something I’d go out of my way for, but it’s a good late-night option since they’re open till 11pm.

author: Ngọc Nga Hồ Trương
review_text: First time visiting Hong Kee and the claypot chicken really impressed me — so flavorful and delicious! Definitely coming back for more! 😋

author: Benjamin Wenisch
review_text: I having a business trip and stay around this area, It was very crowded the first night, and I tested it on the 2nd night. Apart from tourist spots, and it use charcoal to cook, taste is just 3/10. Nothing special. The workers try to scam me when they come to collect money, show me a paper written RM34, after questions them, show me another paper written RM19. Overall it was a good experience, but no next time, consider an overrated food stall.

author: Stefan Nugroho
review_text: Came here on a Wednesday for dinner. We were almost immediately seated, perhaps due to our early arrival (5pm), and thus the restaurant was not completely full and was still available for walk in. After about 2 - 3 mins after being seated, we were immediately approached by a staff that took our order. Depsite us being not ready to order yet, she patiently guided as through and answered our questions. The Yangzhou fried rice was nice, though nothing out of the ordinary, just well made fried rice. The century egg spinach (not in picture) was nice, and was really flavourful. The century egg was nice too, and the quantity was good. We ordered the chilli crab (mud crab) and mantou. The crab was really soft, and the chilli sauce was really delicious and flavourful, without being too spicy. Overall, the food is really delicious. To ensure that you can taste the other dishes, definitely try to consume the weaker tasting foods before eating the stronger tasting ones (e.g. chilli crab). Price is on the high end, but i suppose once in a while it's ok.

author: Francis Leung
review_text: We had a great time at Jumbo Seafood Riverside, Singapore. The private room we got came with a really nice view, which made the whole experience even better. The food was, as always, consistently good. The bamboo clam was huge and absolutely delicious, definitely at a highlight. And of course, the famous chilli crab didn’t disappoint - we had a 1.6 kg one, and it was really, really good. Overall, a solid dining experience with great food and atmosphere.

author: NAPAL PROMPONG
review_text: This is a wonderful restaurant in Singapore. The highlight is definitely the Crab dishes. The meat is sweet and the sauce is perfect. I am Thai, and I am usually picky about Thai food abroad, but the Tom Yum here is fantastic. It tastes like the original flavor from home. Even though the bill was a bit high, I feel it is totally worth it. The experience and the high quality of ingredients make it great value. If you want a delicious seafood meal, you should come here.

author: lay hwa chong
review_text: The service staff were excellent - both at East Coast and Riverwalk branches. Polite, knowledgeable and sharp to observe your needs! The Chinese spinach was pathetic- especially the salted egg cubes which tasted like artificial gum, the century egg is too hard, not “oily” enough. The chilli crab served to its expected standard- I was there 3 weeks ago and the taste is consistent. I was disappointed that I could not use my Dec birthday discount because the Alaskan crab was already discounted and even though we clocked $552.14 in total bill, we could not reach the required $200 after taking out the Alaskan crab. There was only 2 of us. Can you consider extending the voucher till end Jan as an exception? I would have love to use it but I’ll be travelling 22 Dec, returning 23 Jan. Thank you

author: C G
review_text: Haven’t been to Jumbo for several years. We were craving for chilli crabs so Jumbo was our top choice. The chilli crabs were so fresh and sweet. However, they were less spicy than before, we reckoned the outlet caters more to tourists (who might not be able to take spicy dishes). We requested “more spicy” for its Mee Goreng - turned out really good as the squids and prawns were so fresh. As for the stir-fried asparagus with XO sauce, it was flavourful but could have been better if they used the medium-sized ones or fried or steamed them abit longer. Overall, we had a nice meal, and the next time, we will ask for our crabs to be “more spicy”.

author: Lee
review_text: ChiliCrab is a dish, which, can be found throughout Singapore, but I’m told it’s not always prepared the same everywhere. So, after searching, I came across this place and the reviews were impressive. I ordered the Chili Crab, Prawns and the soup. The crab was absolutely delicious. It was fresh and extremely flavorful and had lots of crab meat. The prawns were lightly batted and had good flavor as did the soup. The restaurant is large and offers both indoor and outdoor seating. It sits directly off the water where boats and other water craft travel by showcasing their unique and colorful lighting displays. The staff were friendly and even suggested a few popular dishes. I do recommend making reservations. This is a popular place for tourists to dine and it can get very busy.

author: Morgan Williams
